capacity_gross_kwh.notes: US EX30 (Single Motor Extended Range RWD and Twin Motor Performance AWD): 69 kWh gross. KBB lists 69 kWh for all four 2026 US trims. Cross Country: KBB lists the same 69 kWh pack; DC/AC carried over from the Twin Motor Performance (same hardware, sibling).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: InsideEVs: 64 kWh usable for the US NMC pack. Other pages differ: EV Database 65.0, ArenaEV 65.4, OpenEV 66; auto-data/EVKX 64.

chemistry.notes: InsideEVs: NMC for the US models (Europe entry pack is LFP 51/49 kWh, which our 2026 single-motor variant shows from OpenEV; the Canadian/US Extended Range is the 69 kWh NMC pack: NRCan 420 km matches 261 mi on 69 kWh).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 392 V nominal, 400 V architecture (69 kWh NMC pack).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: no page found states the EX30 navigation trigger. Volvo support for the EX90 (search excerpt) says preconditioning starts automatically when a DC charger is the navigation destination (and can be started manually in the charging view); an EX30 release note excerpt confirms the EX30 has a battery-preconditioning function; EV Database says only that EX30 preconditioning is available. The EX90 also has a manual start, so manual_and_automatic cannot be excluded for the EX30; closest enum chosen from the Google-built-in family (EX40/Polestar 2 pages show only the navigation trigger).

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: up to 153 kW (Volvo US). EV Database also says Volvo claims 153 kW. An InsideEVs test of a 2025 Twin Motor Performance measured about 150 kW at 8% SoC. A Volvo Canada page excerpt shows 175 kW for the larger pack; not used (page not readable).

ac_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: onboard charger rated about 11 kW (about 8 h on 240 V). EV Database: 11 kW standard (22 kW optional in Europe).
